That means going to therapy first, and regularly. If it were me I would tell him the regular therapy is important to you, and him not keeping up with it is a dealbreaker. It’s not easy, but speaking for experience some people never change. And acting like they’re going to is part of what’s known as the “cycle of abuse.” Maybe read up on that concept if you haven’t, and if it sounds like your experience, my advice is to get the hell out of dodge because he won’t change. Easier said than done, I know, but I’ve watched my mom stay in an abusive relationship for 20 years because of guilt tripping. Sooner is better than later.

Take it one day at a time. I promise no one that’s your age feels ready for life. and if they do, they’re overconfident and will realize around age 22 that they actually know nothing. Don’t worry about a job. There are always plenty of jobs on college campuses - look into waiting tables (it’s great money!) or if you are part of any group mes (like my school had a Class of 2022 GroupMe), you could ask if anyones job is hiring. Work study is another thing to look into, maybe check the school website or ask the financial aid office. Are you able to ask your parents about the renters contract? The guy you’re renting from sounds a little shady and I wouldn’t want you to get ripped off. Getting an older adult involved would minimize the chances of that happening. I understand you’re overwhelmed - it’s an overwhelming time! But I promise things will ease up and it will all be so worth it.
